note: TIME.md: waking up (by lead), a bad night in the heat, and the SRO desk clerk renting a room. 'who' marks lead-specific lines.

lines.text: (Teddy) Seven a.m. Somebody's radio. Somebody's always got a radio.
(Teddy) Up. Shower down the hall. Hot water's a rumour.
(Teddy) Dreamt about the car again. Thirty-Fifth Street. Coffee.
(Delphine) Rule one before coffee: count the box. Then coffee.
(Delphine) Afternoon light through the curtain. Nobody banging on the door. A good day.
(Delphine) Feet still hurt. Feet always hurt. Up.
(Nick) Eleni's already at the office. Eleni is always already at the office.
(Nick) Morning. Somewhere a bank is thinking about me. Let it think.
(Nick) Bills in the drawer. Close the drawer. Shave.
(Teddy) Window painted shut. Slept in a puddle. The fan just moved the hot around.
(Teddy) Ninety at midnight. Ninety at six. Ninety is the new zero.
(Delphine) Too hot to sleep, too hot to think. Rule two: think anyway.
(Delphine) Wet towel on the neck, all night. Like sleeping in soup.
(Nick) Even the air-conditioner gave up. Like my bank.
(Nick) I slept on the balcony. Madison Avenue sounds like a war.
Woke up in the dark. Power came back at four. The refrigerator's crying.
Room's four-fifty a night. Bath down the hall. Key back by noon.
Sign the book. Any name. Everybody's Smith on Eighth Avenue.
Fan's extra. Fifty cents. Window opens. Mostly.
No visitors after eleven. That's the rule. I enforce it with my eyes closed.
Corwin's full of old men, but they're quiet. Mostly. Eleven-oh-four sings.
Weekly's twenty-two. Nightly's four-fifty. You look nightly.
Elevator's out. Room's on seven. Builds character.
Cash. In advance. I don't take checks, IOUs, or sad stories.
Can't sleep now. Sirens on the block. Somebody's looking for somebody.
Not now. Too much going on. Sleep's for people with nothing to do.
